llm_findings: The sole flag does not implement the claimed BF16 kernel substitution. Authoritative train.py lines 742–762 define USE_NKI_NGRAM_RMS as a fused FP32 update requiring NGRAM_RMS_FP32; lines 5940–5955 explicitly require --ngram-rms-fp32. Both pinned controls resolve rms_fp32_state_math=False. Thus --nki-ngram-rms alone cannot exercise the supported path as proposed, and nki_rms=True in a configuration log would not establish execution.

Adding --ngram-rms-fp32 would change state storage and update arithmetic as well as kernel execution, contradicting the declared kernel-only causal change against the pinned BF16 control. A revised experiment must isolate the kernel with a compatible matched control, or propose a bounded BF16 kernel implementation.

The novelty evidence contains a direct factual error: research/experiment-log.jsonl includes fs-w4-w896-nki-rms-fp32-r1 with nki_rms=True, 2204 steps and public_val_bpb=0.986947, versus fs-w3-w896-direct-control-r1 at 2188 steps and 0.987568. This is not an exact duplicate of the proposed configuration, but it is relevant prior evidence that must be acknowledged and distinguished.

The proposed throughput and public-BPB thresholds are measurable under the controller's matched seed-42 full-chip experiment, and optimizer kernels are permitted by README.md with no external data, pretrained weights or evaluator changes proposed. These strengths do not resolve the incompatible kernel prerequisite.
